objective: Test one holistic poster direction where custom 茶作 wordmark, tea-process photography, support typography, asymmetrical attention geometry and negative space are designed as one system rather than assembled separately.

concept_readback.poster_geometry: single asymmetrical composition with title block on left and active tea-process photography on right/bottom
concept_readback.support_hierarchy: present as compact left-side secondary block rather than direct under-title caption stacking
concept_readback.custom_wordmark: still calligraphic-adjacent and must be judged by human; not yet accepted as proprietary brand lettering
concept_readback.text_accuracy: not production-authoritative; exact text will be rebuilt in Figma only after concept acceptance
concept_readback.real_photo_subject_fidelity: conceptual handcrafted-tea subject only; does not claim pixel preservation of the existing PHOTO_RAW_LOCKED asset

questions: Does this finally read as a designed poster rather than a photograph with text placed on top?
Is the title-photo-support hierarchy direction worth rebuilding in Figma?
Is the custom 茶作 treatment sufficiently distinctive, or should the poster direction pass while the wordmark itself is redrawn during Figma reconstruction?
